correctness.rationale: The direct full-skeleton augmented chain comparison gives a genuine rational character identity. The externally established two omitted face layers and homology concentration are used with attribution. Invariant p-faces have reversal orientation sign (-1)^floor(p/2), and interval symmetry contributes 1 exactly when r is odd. A complete parity/short-gap enumeration yields C_{n,k}. The module multiplicities are then forced by dimension and trace. Independent cut-face enumeration matched all 45 traces; full GF(2) homology matched all 21 small parameter cases. Finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The full rational C2 eigenspace formula for ordinary k-cut complexes of squared paths is not a theorem in the inspected primary same-object paper, which computes β and complementary-face layers only, nor in the earlier shellability/equivariant work for ordinary paths. Actual research-index comparisons find adjacent but non-dominating objects. The centered connected-subset enumeration is needed to obtain this exact new reflection character. The search cannot prove absence of unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: No search can establish global uniqueness; an unindexed general equivariant Euler formula specialized to squared paths might imply the character.

value.rationale: A complete two-parameter C2 homology representation for the natural squared-path cut complexes is a meaningful equivariant invariant, not determined by the established nonequivariant Betti ranks. A distinct centered-connected-set gap count and signed faces produce concrete ± multiplicities (6/5, 12/13, 31/36 in illustrative cases) with potential use in quotient/equivariant topology. The theorem is all-length, naturally parameterized, and not an arbitrary finite slice.
